"'In fact, if the basis vectors are not orthogonal, then the projection of 'P' onto 'v' will be a linear combination of 'v' and 'w', rather than just 'v' itself. This means that the projection will not be a single point, but rather a line or a plane, depending on the relationship between 'v' and 'w,' said Dr. Doe.

"'So, to summarize, orthogonal projection only works if the two basis vectors 'v' are orthogonal to each other. If they are not, then the projection of a point onto 'v' will not be accurate, and the result will be a linear combination of 'v' and 'w' rather than just 'v' itself,' said Dr. Smith."
